chunks: As for what was narrated by Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stoned, and he did not flog." And they mentioned that ʿAlī عليه السلام stoned in Kūfah and flogged, so Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام rejected that and said: "We do not recognize this." Yūnus said: meaning, we did not administer two punishments to a man for one sin.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What Yūnus mentioned is not in the apparent wording of the report, nor is there in it anything indicating that. Rather, what it contains is that he said, "We do not recognize this," and that may mean that he only intended: we do not recognize that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم stoned and did not flog, because the questioner had previously mentioned two rulings, one of them about the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and the other about Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. There is no stronger reason to direct his statement, "We do not recognize this," to one of them rather than the other. If that is possible, then it does not contradict the reports we mentioned earlier. Then even if it were explicit that he said, "We do not recognize this" among the actions of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, it still would not contradict what we mentioned, because it is possible that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام did not do that since, in his time, there may not have occurred a case in which flogging and stoning were both obligatory together according to the detail we mentioned. And what confirms what we stated regarding the obligation of combining the two penalties is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does this hadith show that stoning and flogging are not combined in the hadd for zinā?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal question concerning whether stoning is accompanied by flogging in the hadd punishment for zinā. It presents a report from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and then a juristic clarification by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan explaining that the report does not conclusively negate combining both penalties in the relevant case.
